newsitem.title: NORWAY: Dyno continues defence in U.S. anti-trust claims.
newsitem.headline: Dyno continues defence in U.S. anti-trust claims.

text.p: Norway's Dyno Industrier AS said on Wednesday its North American explosives subsidiary Dyno Nobel Inc (DNI) continued to defend civil proceedings brought against the company by several customers who are claiming compensation for alleged violations of U.S. anti-trust legislation.
Dyno's statement came after two other defendants cited in the action agreed provisional settlements with the plantiffs.

The plaintiffs, comprising several customer groups, began proceedings against several explosive manufacturers including DNI in 1995. The compensation claims cover all commercial explosives sold by the defendants in the period 1985 to 1993.

"For the past year DNI has been working to defend the plaintiffs' demands. DNI expects that a judgement on whether there are grounds for a class action suit will be given in 1997. Any court proceedings that may ensue are expected to take place in 1998/99," a statement from Dyno said.
"However, Dyno has learnt that two of the defendants cited in the class action have recently agreed to a provisional settlement with the plaintiffs," it said.

If the proposed settlement is accepted by the court, the two explosives manufacturers will pay $18 million and $10 million respectively. An order regarding approval of the proposal is expected in January 1997.
"DNI is still vigorously defending its case," Dyno said.
